source_review.notes: Reviewed eight sources covering edge and cloudlet architecture, fog terminology, constrained networks, cyber-physical reasoning, distributed data, and site reliability. IEEE and NIST DOI metadata confirmed four publication identities and dates; RFC 7228 and the official Google SRE book were retrieved. Sources support durable concepts; no mutable edge-product limit or provider capability is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed event rate, encoded size, disconnected duration, storage lower bound, drain capacity, deadline components, authority epoch, sequence, clock uncertainty, bandwidth reduction, and local-right notation.
Confirmed time, rate, and byte units are converted consistently and deadline terms share units before addition.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The deadline inequality requires bounds matching the claim, not averages.

evidence: Recomputed 500 events/s times 200 bytes times 21,600 seconds as 2,160,000,000 bytes or 2.16 GB decimal.
Recomputed 1,200 events/s times 350 bytes times 64,800 seconds as 27,216,000,000 bytes or 27.216 GB decimal.
Recomputed event backlog 77,760,000 and net drain 800 events/s as 97,200 seconds or 27 hours.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All storage and drain values are explicitly lower-bound or idealized calculations before overhead, burst, retries, and failure.

evidence: Verified B_min=lambda s T from constant admitted rate, mean encoded size, and isolation duration.
Verified reconnect net drain mu-lambda and finite clearance only when mu exceeds continuing production lambda.
Verified the additive end-to-end deadline budget only for bounded sequential path components and a declared safety margin.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Models do not cover stochastic size, bandwidth variation, parallel paths, clock faults, or physical dynamics without additional evidence.

evidence: Reviewed network delay beyond hard deadline, six- and eighteen-hour isolation, full buffer, drain slower than production, and fleet reconnect herd.
Reviewed stale command after emergency epoch, clock reset, twin disagreement, aggregation hiding excursion, old hardware, and legacy replay.
Reviewed stolen device, shared secret, malicious update, central compromise, island partition, false sensor, stuck actuator, and retirement.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cases span timing, storage, consistency, physical state, fleet compatibility, security, privacy, recovery, and public safety.

evidence: Traced command authority and expiry, physical interlocks, local rights conservation, priority buffer reserve, device-scoped identity, update compatibility, and residency through examples and answers.
Confirmed event delivery, gateway state, twin state, command acknowledgement, and physical effect remain distinct.
invariant_checking.notes: Reconnection and restoration require digital, business, and physical reconciliation.

evidence: Reviewed the storage lower-bound derivation and confirmed all units and constant-rate assumptions are explicit.
Reviewed the drain argument and confirmed backlog cannot clear at service less than or equal to ongoing production without contract change.
Reviewed the 20-ms interlock counterexample and confirmed an observed 80-ms remote path cannot satisfy that control deadline.
proof_review.notes: No gateway, twin, secure-boot, or cloud-health signal is presented as proof of physical correctness.

evidence: Audited uses of local, authoritative, current, safe, bounded, trusted, secure, synchronized, healthy, physical, compatible, and retired.
Verified models, mechanisms, identity claims, policies, observations, simulations, and physical evidence retain explicit scopes.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Digital representations and acknowledgements are never equated with the physical asset.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter prescribes hardware, field, connectivity, compromise, reconnect, and lifecycle tests but reports no executed edge fleet, machine, flood barrier, or public-warning experiment.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed physical authority, tier responsibilities, disconnected operation, commands and facts, twins, clocks, buffering, drain, bandwidth reduction, lifecycle placement, rights, identity, physical access, supply chain, fleet heterogeneity, legacy trust, connectivity, planes, inference, observation, retirement, and testing for coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed machine interlock, offline depot, clinic rights, stale valve command, twin conflict, hazardous aggregation, reconnect herd, stolen device, old-hardware update, and legacy actuator gateway. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth timing, authority, fleet, and physical-world reasoning, sixteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar international coastal flood-control transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks and calculations do not constitute a live edge fleet, disconnected clinic, industrial actuator, device-compromise, coastal flood, or public-safety experiment.
